title: Geology Collection Conceptual Data Model (GCDM) Glossary
scopeNote: The Geology Collections Conceptual Data Model Glossary is a terminological resource containing terms with definitions for concepts related to Geological Collections.
historyNote: Transformed into KOS platform format from the Geological Collections Conceptual Data Model (GCDM) tabular glossary.

terms.label: Alternate Name
terms.definition: An alternate lexical label to the preferred term for an entity.
terms.scopeNote: Alternate names are informal and unregulated by an authoritative body such as the International Mineralogical Association.

terms.label: Astromaterial
terms.definition: Any material that meets one of the following conditions: 1) Recovered from space, 2) Extraterrestrial in origin, 3) Paragenetically linked to a material that meets condition 1 or 2 or occurs as a direct product of some process involving an astromaterial.

terms.label: Authority
terms.definition: Identifies the entity responsible for assigning and maintaining a formalized classification system

terms.label: Biostratigraphic Unit
terms.definition: Geologic units defined or characterized on the basis of their contained fossils. Biostratigraphic units exist only where the particular diagnostic feature or attribute on which they are based has been identified.

terms.label: Chronostratigraphic Unit
terms.definition: Bodies of rocks, layered or unlayered, that are defined between specified stratigraphic horizons which represent specified intervals of geologic time.

terms.label: Classification
terms.definition: Activity involving grouping similar or related things together; separating dissimilar or unrelated things; and arranging the resulting groups in a logical and helpful sequence

terms.label: Classification Code
terms.definition: Encoded classification of an object represented by a graphical symbol that conforms to an encoding scheme defined as part of the classification scheme
terms.scopeNote: Dana Number, Linnaean Taxonomy does not use a classification code, rather just a single latin term

terms.label: Classification Family
terms.definition: A thematic grouping of related classification series that treat the same domain; a labelled collection asserting that its member series are alternative or complementary treatments of one subject, without imposing internal order or hierarchy.
terms.scopeNote: SKOS-aligned label in the general hierarchical classification model. Examples — Mineral: “Mineral classification” grouping the Nickel–Strunz, Dana and Fleischer series; Lithostratigraphic: “Lithostratigraphic classification” grouping the North American Stratigraphic Code and International Stratigraphic Guide series.

terms.label: Classification Item Relation
terms.definition: The directed parent–child edge linking a child classification term to its parent; the set of these edges constitutes the hierarchy. One parent by default (monohierarchy); permitting more than one parent yields a polyhierarchy.
terms.scopeNote: Reifies the skos:broader / skos:narrower edge between Classification Terms. The edge is generic (not committed to is-a), so it carries both taxonomic and mereological hierarchies. Examples — Mineral (taxonomic): Quartz → Quartz group → Silica family; Lithostratigraphic (mereological): Navajo Sandstone → Glen Canyon Group.

terms.label: Classification Level
terms.definition: A stratified tier comprised of nodes with a shared level of granularity in a hierarchy. The distance of a level from the root is expressed as the Depth. The identifier (label) assigned to a level is referred to as the Rank.

terms.label: Classification Name
terms.definition: A formalized name belonging to a classification system maintained by an authoritative body.

terms.label: Classification Rank
terms.definition: An identifier assigned to a classification level commonly expressed using a numeric identifier or lexical label

terms.label: Classification Rank Relation
terms.definition: The ordering relation between two classification ranks, stating which tier sits immediately above another. Present only when a scheme is ranked; omitted entirely for unranked schemes such as cladistic or purely lithologic trees.
terms.scopeNote: Orders Classification Levels by Depth. Examples — Mineral: Class > Subclass, Family > Species; Lithostratigraphic: Group > Formation, Formation > Member.

terms.label: Classification Scheme
terms.definition: A method of organization according to a set of pre-established principles, usually characterized by a notation system and a hierarchical structure of relationships among the entities. Defines structure and organization of a classification including the hierarchical ranks

terms.label: Classification Series
terms.definition: The time-ordered set of successive versions (editions or revisions) of a single classification, expressing that one classification persists and evolves through versions while retaining its identity.
terms.scopeNote: Complements Classification Version (a single versioned instance): a Series is the ordered set of Versions. Examples — Mineral: “Dana” (6th 1892 → 8th 1997), “Nickel–Strunz” (through the 10th, 2009); Lithostratigraphic: “North American Stratigraphic Code” (1983 → 2005 → 2021).

terms.label: Classification System
terms.definition: Terminological resource which has characteristics of mutual exclusiveness and exhaustiveness to aggregate data to a pre-prescribed level of specialization for a specific purpose. Extends the classification scheme concept to include the value domain used to populate a classification scheme

terms.label: Classification Term
terms.definition: A single concept in a classification system or scheme at any hierarchical level.

terms.label: Classification Version
terms.definition: A versioned instance of a classification scheme
terms.scopeNote: In a version, the categories of the classification version are split, aggregated or regrouped to provide additions or alternatives to the standard order and structure of the base version.

terms.label: Collection Object
terms.definition: A physical object that belongs to a museum collection.

terms.label: Compound Specimen
terms.definition: A collection object comprised of one or more discernible parts, called specimen parts, unified by physical attachment. The object's identity is determined by its specimen parts, which are distinguished from one another within a specific context.

terms.label: Compound Specimen Model
terms.definition: A conceptual data model in which a single physical object, a compound specimen, is composed of and defined by its specimen parts.

terms.label: Concept
terms.definition: Unit of knowledge created by a unique combination of characteristics

terms.label: Conceptual Model
terms.definition: An abstract model or representation of data for a particular domain or field of study, independent of any specific software or information system.

terms.label: Continuent
terms.definition: A continuant is an entity that persists, endures, or continues to exist through time while maintaining its identity. Continuants can preserve their identity even while gaining and losing material parts.

terms.label: Data Model
terms.definition: Graphical and/or lexical representation of data, specifying their properties, structure, and interrelationships

terms.label: Depth
terms.definition: The numeric distance of a nested level from the root of a hierarchy in a stratified classification scheme

terms.label: Determination
terms.definition: The identity of a specimen represented by a name based on formal criteria evaluated by a domain expert. In biological collections, the determination is represented by a taxonomic classification, primarily a genus and species (e.g., Vulpes vulpes, Accipiter cooperii). In the geosciences domain, examples of determination include Almandine, Granite, and Plantae.

terms.label: Feature
terms.definition: abstraction of real world phenomena

terms.label: Feature of Interest
terms.definition: A feature of interest is an abstraction of a real-world phenomenon \which is being sampled or transformed in an act of Sampling..
terms.scopeNote: A feature of interest is defined in terms of its properties, which are qualifiable, quantifiable, observable, or operable qualities.

terms.label: Formal Name
terms.definition: A name sanctioned by an authoritative body (e.g. naming authority, formal classification system) based on a defined set of unambiguous criteria and belonging to a formal nomenclature

terms.label: Fossil
terms.definition: Any remains, trace, or imprint of a plant or animal preserved in the Earth's crust since some past geologic or prehistoric time; loosely, any evidence of past life.

terms.label: Geochronologic Boundary
terms.definition: Temporal boundaries defined with reference to some geologic evidence such as, for instance, fossil appearance/disappearance or significant change in local rock lithology.

terms.label: Geochronologic Interpretation
terms.definition: An interpretation made by a geologist of the age of a specimen made by statistical analysis of a single collection of observations. A specimen may have multiple geochronological interpretations made on it, each related to a different observation collection.

terms.label: Geochronologic Unit
terms.definition: A specialized time ordinal interval used to subdivide geologic time based on a corresponding chronostratigraphic unit.

terms.label: Geochronology
terms.definition: The science of determining absolute ages of geological events and Earth materials. The primary technique utilizes radioactive isotopes and the production and accumulation of radiogenic daughter isotopes naturally present on Earth. It can be applied to various samples, including rocks, minerals, and biological materials.

terms.label: Geologic Environment
terms.definition: Physical conditions found on the Earth's surface, which are determined by factors such as climate, tectonics, physiography, geography and within the Earth's interior, determined by pressure, temperature, chemical environment, and tectonics.

terms.label: Geologic Event
terms.definition: An identifiable event during which one or more geologic processes act to modify geologic entities.

terms.label: Geologic Event Environment
terms.definition: The physical setting within which a Geologic Event takes place.

terms.label: Geologic Feature
terms.definition: A physical or conceptual feature that is hypothesized to exist coherently in the Earth and that results from geological processes.

terms.label: Geologic Material
terms.definition: An amount of matter primarily (dominantly) having parts created by geologic processes and can include minor parts that are not of geologic origin, such as organic material, and can be solid, fluid, or a mix

terms.label: Geologic Material Relation
terms.definition: A perceived association between two geologic materials described by a relation predicate.

terms.label: Geologic Object
terms.definition: An amount of matter primarily having parts created by geologic processes and composed of one or more Specimen Parts unified by physical attachment. Geologic Objects may include minor parts not of geologic origin, such as organic material or synthetic material generated as a close approximation.

terms.label: Geologic Process
terms.definition: A natural process that affects the geologic record by acting upon one geologic entity to produce another geologic entity at a later time.
terms.source: Neuendorf et al. (2005); Richard et al. (2007)

terms.label: Geologic Structure
terms.definition: A pattern in a rock body (foliation, fold) or a feature occurring between rock bodies (contact, fracture).

terms.label: Geologic Timescale
terms.definition: A temporal reference system that subdivides all the time since Earth formed into named intervals (units) of abstract time and subdivides all the rocks formed since Earth formed into the successions of rock formed during each particular interval of time

terms.label: Geologic Unit
terms.definition: A body of rock that persists through time, forming a discrete and definable unit. Geologic units are identified by their geometric, compositional, and internal structural characteristics, as well as their spatio-temporal relations with other rock bodies.
terms.scopeNote: Geologic Units Include both formal units (i.e. formally adopted and named in an official lexicon) and informal units (i.e. named but not promoted to the lexicon) and unnamed units (i.e. recognisable and described and delineable in the field but not otherwise formalised).

terms.label: Geologic Unit Type
terms.definition: A scheme that specifies concepts used to categorize types of geologic units. Unit types are differentiated based on their defining composition, temporal context, or other physical properties.

terms.label: Geological Specimen
terms.definition: A collection object comprised in part of geologic material

terms.label: Half-life
terms.definition: The length of time over which half the atoms of radioactive isotopes decay. The half-life remains constant as the number of atoms is reduced, resulting in an exponential rate of decay

terms.label: Hierarchy
terms.definition: Concept system in which all concepts are related in hierarchical relations that form a partial ordering

terms.label: Identification
terms.definition: Process of recognizing an entity in a particular domain as distinct from other entities.

terms.label: Indentifier
terms.definition: Sequence of characters permanently associated with an object or aspect of an object for reference to uniquely identify it in a specified context

terms.label: Interpreted Age
terms.definition: The age of a geologic event that resulted in the formation of a geologic material that is expressed numerically and based on the results of a dating technique such as radiometric dating or dendrochronology.

terms.label: Law of Superposition
terms.definition: A general law upon which all geologic chronology is based, where younger lithostratigraphic units lie atop older lithostratigraphic units
terms.scopeNote: In any sequence of layered rocks, sedimentary or extrusive volcanic, that has not been overturned, the youngest stratum is at the top and the oldest at the base; i.e., each bed is younger that the bed beneath, but older than the bed above it

terms.label: Linnaean Taxonomy
terms.definition: A classification system for grouping both living and extinct organisms governed by the International Commission on Zoological Nomenclature. Generally, the parent-child relationships in the Linnaean hierarchy represent the lineage evolution between species.

terms.label: Lithodemic Unit
terms.definition: A defined body of predominantly intrusive, highly deformed, and (or) highly metamorphosed rock, distinguished and delimited based on rock characteristics
terms.scopeNote: Lithodemic units do not follow the law of superposition.

terms.label: Lithology
terms.definition: (a) The description of rocks, especially in hand specimens and outcrops, based on characteristics such as color, mineralogic composition, and grain size. (b) The physical character of a rock.

terms.label: Lithostratigraphic Unit
terms.definition: A defined body of sedimentary, extrusive igneous, metasedimentary, or metavolcanic strata that is distinguished and delimited based on lithic characteristics and stratigraphic position
terms.scopeNote: Lithostratigraphic units obey the law of superposition.

terms.label: Logical Data Model
terms.definition: A data model that includes all entities and the relationships among them based on the structures identified in a conceptual data model and that specifies all attributes for each entity.

terms.label: Lower Temporal Boundary
terms.definition: The maximum limit or latest point in time allowed for a specific event, process, or condition to occur or be considered within a given context or timescale.
terms.scopeNote: Equivalent to time:startTime and oldest age

terms.label: Magnetostratigraphic Unit
terms.definition: Bodies of rock strata unified by similar magnetic characteristics which allow them to be differentiated from adjacent strata.

terms.label: Material Category
terms.definition: A value belonging to a top-level, generalized categorization scheme for specimen parts where each specimen part belongs to and only one material category. For any given collection, these material categories should comprehensively account for all parts found across every specimen in that collection.

terms.label: Material Entity
terms.definition: An entity that exists in full during the length of time of its existence, persists through this time while maintaining its identity and has no temporal parts.

terms.label: Material Sample
terms.definition: A physical result of a sampling (or subsampling) event. Material samples are typically collected and either preserved or destructively processed.

terms.label: Mine
terms.definition: A work for excavating minerals using pits, shafts, levels, tunnels, etc., as opposed to a quarry, where the whole excavation is open. In general, the existence of a mine is determined by the mode in which the mineral is obtained, not by its chemical or geological character. The term also includes only excavations for their minerals or valuable mineral deposits.

terms.label: Mineral
terms.definition: A naturally occurring element or chemical compound that is normally crystalline and formed due to geological processes

terms.label: Mineraloid
terms.definition: An amount of amorphous material; commonly the product of rapid cooling of melted material. Includes natural glasses in Earth and extraterrestrial material, some biogenic mineral products, and anthromophomorphic manufactured material.

terms.label: Model
terms.definition: A simplified representation or abstraction of a system, process, or concept

terms.label: Monohierarchy
terms.definition: Hierarchical arrangement of concepts in a classification scheme in which each concept can have only one broader concept at the level immediately above.

terms.label: Museum Collection
terms.definition: An object aggregate that has as member parts a material sample that is located in a museum as a result of a process of curation.

terms.label: Name
terms.definition: Primary means of identification of objects and concepts for humans
terms.scopeNote: The term ‘Name’ refers to any label assigned to a specimen for identification, including both terms that belong to a formal classification system and informal alternate terms.

terms.label: Naming Authority
terms.definition: A registration authority that allocates names according to specified rules.

terms.label: Natural Geomorphological Feature
terms.definition: A natural geomorphological feature that has been created by natural Earth processes.

terms.label: Object
terms.definition: An object is a maximal causally unified material entity, meaning b is a material entity which is such that its material parts are tied together in such a way that, in environments typical for entities of the type in question

terms.label: Object Aggregate
terms.definition: A material entity consisting exactly of a plurality of objects as continuant (member) parts at all times at which the object aggregate exists.

terms.label: Ontology
terms.definition: Specification of concrete or abstract things, and the relationships among them, in a prescribed domain of knowledge

terms.label: Petrographic Province
terms.definition: A broad area in which similar igneous rocks are formed during the same period of igneous activity.

terms.label: Physical Collection
terms.definition: Designates an aggregated group of tangible objects with a focal characteristic assembled and maintained by an individual or organization over time. A collection comprises multiple items that are conceptually or physically arranged together for a specific purpose and audience, according to a collection plan

terms.label: Physical Data Model
terms.definition: A technical representation detailing how data is physically organized and constrained within a database system, focusing on tables, columns, and constraints rather than entities and attributes.
terms.source: Agile Data Warehousing for the Enterprise, 2016

terms.label: Physical Object
terms.definition: Items of a material nature that are units for documentation and have physical boundaries that separate them completely in an objective way from other objects.

terms.label: Physiographic Feature
terms.definition: A natural feature of the solid surface of the Earth or other planetary body.

terms.label: Physiographic Province
terms.definition: A region in which all parts are similar in geologic structure and climate and which has consequently had a unified geomorphic history; a region whose pattern of relief features or landforms differs significantly from adjacent regions

terms.label: Province
terms.definition: Any large area or region considered as a whole, all parts characterized by similar features or a history differing significantly from adjacent areas.

terms.label: Quarry
terms.definition: An open or surface mineral working, usually for extracting building stone, such as slate, limestone, etc. It is distinguished from a mine because a quarry usually is open at the top and front, and, in ordinary use of the term, by the character of the material extracted.

terms.label: Radioactive Decay
terms.definition: The process where an unstable parent isotope loses particles from its atomic nucleus (decay) to form a daughter isotope (product) at a constant rate

terms.label: Radiometric Age
terms.definition: Geologic age expressed in years determined by quantitatively measuring radioactive elements and their decay products

terms.label: Radiometric Dating
terms.definition: Proper chronological placement of a feature, object, or happening in the geologic time scale without reference to its absolute age.

terms.label: Regional Timescale
terms.definition: A family of geologic timescales based on the strata and fossil record observed in a specific area, typically at the country or regional level.

terms.label: Relation Predicate
terms.definition: The term describing the nature of the relationship between two specimen parts within the scope of a compound specimen

terms.label: Relative Age
terms.definition: The geologic age of a fossil organism, rock, or geologic feature or event defined relative to other organisms, rocks, or features or events rather than in terms of years.

terms.label: Relative Dating
terms.definition: Proper chronological placement of a feature, object, or happening in the geologic time scale without reference to its absolute age.

terms.label: Rock
terms.definition: A consolidated or unconsolidated aggregate of mineral grains consisting of one or more mineral species and having some degree of chemical and mineralogic constancy

terms.label: Sample
terms.definition: A feature which is intended to be representative of a `FeatureOfInterest` on which `Observations` may be made.

terms.label: Sampling Event
terms.definition: An activity of Sampling carries out a (Sampling) Procedure to create or transform one or more Samples.

terms.label: Sampling Feature
terms.definition: The feature of interest a sample is intended to be representative of.

terms.label: Sampling Feature Type
terms.definition: The nature of the feature such as whether the feature is the result of natural processes.

terms.label: Sampling Location
terms.definition: The geographic place where a sampling event takes place.

terms.label: Sedimentary Facies
terms.definition: A lithologic variant in a sedimentary unit, typically related to spatial variation in the original depositional environment or subsequent diagenetic environment.

terms.label: Semantic Interoperability
terms.definition: Ability for data shared by systems to be understood at the level of fully defined domain concepts

terms.label: Simple Specimen
terms.definition: A collection object identified by a single determination without discernible parts.

terms.label: Simple Specimen Model
terms.definition: The conceptual model for the digital representation of physical specimens where each entity is  characterized by one and only one determination without any discrenible parts.

terms.label: Source Role
terms.definition: A term describing the role played by the source specimen part in a specimen part relation

terms.label: Specimen Name
terms.definition: Refers to any name assigned to a specimen at the object level (before atomization into specimen parts). Specimen names are often written as compound terms, a concatenation of multiple informal and formal identifiers.

terms.label: Specimen Part
terms.definition: Physically discernible and proximal parts of a compound specimen identified by a single determination based on physical and chemical exclusivity relative to the parent specimen.
terms.scopeNote: A specimen part belongs to one and only one material category and defined in terms of role and proportion relative to the parent compound specimen.

terms.label: Specimen Part Proportion
terms.definition: Refers to the qualitative or quantitative representation of the abundance of a Specimen Part within a parent Compound Specimen.

terms.label: Specimen Part Relation
terms.definition: A described uni-directional association between two specimen parts, a source and target, within the scope of the parent compound specimen. A relation is defined from the perspective of the source specimen part and described using a relation predicate.
terms.scopeNote: One specimen part may be associated with multiple specimen part relations in either role. Each specimen part relation only exists between the two member specimen parts.

terms.label: Specimen Part Relation Type
terms.definition: A term from a controlled vocabulary to describe the specimen part relation

terms.label: Specimen Part Role
terms.definition: Specifies the relationship between a Specimen Part and its parent compound specimen. Roles are dependent upon both the part and parent object. For instance, a rock (material category) within the parent specimen plays the role of clast and is dependent on both the specimen part and the parent specimen for its existence.

terms.label: Stratigraphic Column
terms.definition: (a) A composite diagram that shows in a single column the subdivisions of part or all of geologic time or the sequence of stratigraphic units of a given locality or region (the oldest at the bottom and the youngest at the top, with dips adjusted to the horizontal) so arranged as to indicate their relations to the subdivisions of geologic time and their relative positions to each other (b) The vertical or chronologic arrangement or sequence of rock units portrayed in a geologic column.

terms.label: Stratigraphic Unit
terms.definition: A body of rock established as a distinct entity in the classification of the rocks, based on any of the properties or attributes or combinations thereof that rocks possess.International Stratigraphic Guide

terms.label: Stratigraphy
terms.definition: The description of all rock bodies forming the Earth’s crust and their organization into distinctive, useful, mappable units based on their inherent properties or attributes in order to establish their distribution and relationship in space and their succession in time, and to interpret geologic history.

terms.label: Target Role
terms.definition: A term describing the role played by the target specimen part in a specimen part relation

terms.label: Tectonic Province
terms.definition: Groups of provinces linked by a common tectonic history are designated tectonic provinces. Tectonic provinces may contain a collection of sedimentary, igneous, structural, metamorphic, and metallogenic provinces.

terms.label: Tectonic Setting
terms.definition: A geologic event environment defined by relationships to tectonic plates on or in the Earth.

terms.label: Tectonostratigraphic Unit
terms.definition: Geologic unit defined on basis of structural or deformation features, mutual relations, origin or historical evolution. Contained material may be igneous, sedimentary, or metamorphic.
terms.scopeNote: Concept referred to as a lithotectonic unit in source

terms.label: Temporal Coordinate System
terms.definition: A temporal system where time positions are measurements expressed numerically on a scale

terms.label: Temporal Ordinal Reference System
terms.definition: An ordered system of named intervals
terms.scopeNote: Each interval belongs to a rank in a mono-hierarchical structure where each parent is divided into one or many children of the next finer rank. This structure allows the set of temporal positions are uniquely ordered relative to the reference system.

terms.label: Terrane
terms.definition: A fault-bounded area or region with different layers, rock structures, and geologic history from nearby areas that are not connected to them by unconformable contacts or changes in the rock's surface.

terms.label: Time Interval
terms.definition: A temporal entity with an extent or duration

terms.label: Time Ordinal Interval
terms.definition: A named or identified interval from a temporal ordinal reference system

terms.label: Unconsolidated
terms.definition: Unconsolidated earth material is an 'earth material' that is constituted by an aggregate of solid particles but is not consolidated into a 'rock' it self.

terms.label: Upper Temporal Boundary
terms.definition: The lower limit or earliest point in time allowed for a specific event, process, or condition to occur or be considered within a given context or timescale.
terms.scopeNote: Equivalent to time:endTime and youngest age

terms.label: Value Set
terms.definition: The range of values used to populate a classification scheme (or classification scheme variant)
terms.scopeNote: Equivalent to the range includes property of a classification system
